[quote=the_crystalline_empire;58962906]The interior of the house was finely decorated, not too lavish but still it was clear that this was a palace or at least a grand house. Paintings hung from every wall, and fine furniture filled the halls. A central courtyard at the center of the house, and of course various state rooms presented themselves through open doors on this the first floor. They did not walk for a long while, merely passing through the front door and entering a side room that stood at the front of the house. This room was a richly frescoed room, with light colored wall paper and gilded furniture. A clock stood on a mantel, ticking away lazily. Strangely enough there weren't any servants visibly present, to which Mij made a comment.

"You won't be meeting any of the staff or bureaucrats today unfortunately, it's a mandatory work holiday for them. One must keep the bureaucrats happy, you get far more things done that way," she stated dryly, before motioning for him to sit.

"Now do tell me, what brings you this far from home?" she enquired, sitting herself in a chair opposite of Julius.[/quote]

[i]I sat down, more nervous than confident. I didn't like the dry tone, but I also remembered the Rex's threat should I fail. I took out the telegram from the Rex and slid it her way. The contents of the telegram were unknown to me, as I was told not to open it. It read as followed:

"To the esteemed ruler of Thyven,

Long have we waited. For the past 10 years, we have been rebuilding after a great civil war. The Kingdom of Vers would like to officially join hands with Thyven in a mutual military or trade alliance that benefits all. I have dispatched my third cousin, Julius Valerian Cassiodorus Vers Allusia, as my diplomatic envoy. He shall stay as long as you deem him welcome. Should he fail in his mission, do as you please with him. May you live a long and prosperous life, and may this meeting lead to others in the future.

Signed,
Rex Lucianus Honorius Maximus Vers Reyvers XIV of Vers
Adjutant Asseylum Vers Allusia of Vers"
[/i]

Adjutant Asseylum Vers Allusia of Vers"
[/i][/quote]

She read the letter, smiled, and then put it to the side, before replying, "Given the nature of his majesty's request, in regards to a military alliance, well Thýven is already part of three, and as for an economic alliance, I really do not feel a desire to invite you into the mess that is THEP...that is the Thýven-Hydronia Economic Pact."

She paused, weighing her words before continuing.

"Of course this is not a rejection, I should add. I'd advise for at least the terms of a military alliance that you approach our partner to the South of us, High Albany, they are the head of the White Sea Organisation, a local military organisation focused primarily on protecting local interests, which I feel would suit your nation more than THEP, which is currently engaged in a costly war against a group of terrorists on Shamat," she stated once more before pausing and then restarting.

"As for economic alliance, I would be more than happy to have you meet Isef Drimmons, who is not only the head of the Department of Trade but also of THEP," she replied, finally leaning back in her chair to gauge Julius' reply.

[quote=lavinsworth_united_islands;58961464][b]Establishment of the Erene Economic and Humanitarian Pact (EEHP)[/b]

[i]Today the Minister of the United Lavian Republic is sending out a call for a economic pact spanning the world to not only better connect the nations of Erene, but to also help deny monetary or political gain to those who violate human rights and suppress their people. This pact looks to help better connect the world economically and ethically through the following points, to be made clear or adjusted once nations have adequately joined and the debate process can begin, with a set of ground principals to base off of:[/i]

[b]1. Open borders and ports:[/b] The members of the EEHP will share open borders with each other. In practice, this means citizens of each nation will have the privilege of traveling passport and visa free, with the potential of streamlined immigration between members. This brings the benefit of increased tourism and a larger sense of collaboration between members. Members will also have open port policies with the other members, meaning a decrease in docking fees allowing for ease of business between members.

[b]2. Sharing of business licenses and integration of international safety standards:[/b]Members of the EEHP will share the same level of safety standards and regulations, thus allowing for companies to be licensed in one country and use that license across all nations in the EEHP rather than having to get multiple licenses and concern themselves with different laws and safety standards. This will not only help companies, but also ensure that ethical practices in EEHP countries will be encouraged.

[b]3. Sharing of innovations and breakthroughs:[/b] EEHP members will share practices with each other to not only benefit members, but also build a better Erene for current and future generations. This includes the sharing of the best industry practices to prevent environmental impact via pollution, deforestation, over-farming/fishing, and also share stake in world wide conservation projects of natural habitats and cultural sites. Breakthroughs in industries will also be shared between nations, allowing for better industry practices across the world.

[b]4. Implement tariffs and import restrictions on nations that promote unethical practices or undemocratic principals:[/b] Membership in the EEHP not only looks to benefit the nations in it, but to benefit the world via lowering and hopefully removing reliance on fascist nations or those ruled by dictators (not including constitutional monarchies, parliamentary monarchies, or similar governments that practice the basics of democracy and good humanitarian practices.) Stemming the reliance on child labor and the exploitation of workers via taxing the imports from these nations will hopefully encourage the nations that use these practices to pivot to more sustainable and humanitarian based practices. The first and second points of this charter will also help ease the transition from the companies that use these practices by making the shipment of resources between members cheaper and more accessible to companies in the member nations.

[b]5. Promotion of humanitarian practices:[/b] Humanitarian laws to be practiced and imposed in member nations include but are not limited to: 
- Laws against exclusion of people based on their race, gender, sexuality, or religion
- Freedom of religion
- Freedom of speech (specifics to be determined by the founding members)
- Minimum wage laws (to be determined by the individual country)
- Limit on maximum hours of work before overtime pay begins
- Free school for at least up until grade/year 8 in less developed countries, and free high school for the more developed countries (university/college is up to the individual country to decide)
These policies will be helped via an aid fund to be contributed to by each government via a number of % of their GDP to help other member nations with disasters or modernization

Invited members include:
[nation]Indonocaismnic[/nation]
[nation]Sikirsk[/nation]
[nation]United Hydronia[/nation]
[nation]New Westmore[/nation]
[nation]Goleornacha Roleplay Posts[/nation]
Membership is not restricted to these nations and the ULR encourages people to apply for membership, this list is simply a list of countries the ULR knows are respectable and has good relations with already. It should also be clarified that this will not interject with any military alliances, however if one member attacks another, or a nation attacks a member and another member state joins the attack, the attacking member will be removed from the pact if the member does not provide ample reason for such action.[/quote]

[b]Hijack[/b]
Early in the morning of 30th March, a group of Sal-Baliz operatives in Thýven made their way to the airport. Disguised as tourists, they split up into three small teams, each team carrying tickets to a different plane. These tickets had been acquired from the Armed Republic of Sikirsk during its final days in power. The teams swiftly made their way through airport security.

You may be wondering how a group of hijackers managed to get past the vigilant security of Thýven. Well, there was no reason for them to be stopped. No guns, no drugs, no knives. They were armed with nothing but their fists; however, this was all they needed. Ever since childhood, these men had been training to hijack flights. They had spent hours learning to master hand-to-hand combat in order to take control of the plane as easily as possible.

At 7:30 a.m., the first plane took off, heading west, but was soon hijacked and taken northeast towards Hydronia instead. The orders of these hijackers were to crash into the Kazaruk base, where five prisoners were being held. The plan was to kill the prisoners before they could reveal any information. The second plane took off at 8:00 a.m. and headed towards Etherniasti, with the intent to crash into a skyscraper in Port Thriump. The final plane took off at 9:15 a.m., initially heading south but was quickly turned back around and headed straight for Tharkønn.The Sal-Baliz claimed that the reason the ARoS collapsed was the invasion by Thýven, so this attack was considered punishment for the brief war.

Panic spread across these nations as word got out that three planes had been hijacked. The Sal-Baliz wanted to make a big strike, and here it was.

[b]Expansion, For the Common Defense[/b]

  With peace restored between Thýven and Sikirsk, and the blockade being lifted from that nation, the government and people of Thýven have begun to look towards ensuring the security of that region, while also expanding Thývens economic and power strength. The move labelled in Parliament as The ONEThýven Policy would lay out a plan for future growth into West Shamat via gradual military expansion into the region, thereby allowing for a superseding of local powers in favor of Thýven based powers. 

  While the plan laid out a roadmap of 4-years of expansion, in reality, the expansion had already begun on day 1 of the peace treaty being signed. In the treaty Sikirsk granted Thýven permission to establish a base of 25,000 soldiers on the mainland near Sikirsk. This was the plan, indeed approximately to the west of Sikirsks main Island just north of Wendana, recon groups had determined that the jutting portion of land, populated by approximately 560,000 people scattered in various small villages and a small port city that seemed to go by the name of Al-immír, was an appropriate region to establish the base. 

  As a result of this, the blockade fleet would leave Sikirsks waters within the 48 hour timeline given on the treaty, heading for the shores of Western Shamat not too far nearby. While the blockade fleet was not large enough to gather the entire peninsula into its maws without establishing a wide radius that would make any blockade unfeasible, the mere presence of Thývens ships off the shore of Al-immír caused great panic in the region as the local militia began to gather their forces.

In the meantime a second force would be directed at another peninsula, this time to the south of Wendana and the ULR territories on the western shore of Shamat, the peninsula was a well defended and strategic position in the opinion of the government of Thýven, and they were right, it also was relatively uninhabited, and could provide a link to Shamat and then Sal-Baliz. As a result the 12,000 man force would set out from Thýven to take the peninsula.

  While concerns were raised on the matter of these operations and their scope, the Monarchy would be in full backing, already establishing plans to appoint members of the royal family as governors of the future newly acquired lands. 

  War was a messy thing, and indeed the pushback from Al-Immír and its surrounding villages to the forces of Thýven would devolve into a form of guerilla warfare that would make any troop landing almost impossible. As a result Thýven would turn to its air-force for back up support, issuing strike orders against the villages and city over the night of the third week of fighting against the villagers. The bombings would be successful in damaging critical infrastructure, although, it would unfortunately provide more ground for guerrillas to hide. 

   

  Unfortunately as the sun rose over Al-Immír the position of Thýven was not much changed, forcing the armed forces to temporarily halt the invasion until a new plan could be drawn up. Taking advantage of resources from Hydronia, which had been allocated for the war of Sikirsk, the armed forces would resume their operations by the next day, launching a precision strike program against water-supply and crop regions. In the areas that the troops were able to get a foothold, immediate blocks on water resources would begin. 

In the meantime far more success had been found in the inhabiting of the peninsula, with a more peaceful set of events occurring there than in Al-Immír. Due to the relatively empty nature of the peninsula, save for some ancient ruins, the forces of Thýven were able to take the peninsula in a little more than two weeks, managing to only have to fight an angry farmer and some villagers who had gathered there to watch the fight. The territory was of fine form and good consistent nature for a permanent settlement, and word would be sent back to Thýven regarding this. 

Questions would begin to arise over the feasibility of taking Al-Immír, with many stating that it made no sense to have a territory that far north, however, it was clear that the government of Thýven had no intention of letting Shamat rest, the matter with Sikirsk had only solidified this issue, with queen Mij Drs stating Thýven must take the lead in ensuring the security of its allies and of Shamat,.

As a result heavier bombings would be issued against Al-Immír, razing homes, hospitals, schools, and whatever buildings could be turned to rubble. In the third week a blockade was formally instituted of the port, and the fishermen's boats would be bombed or burned by the landing forces which had finally been deployed en masse.

Thýven didnt usually use swarm tactics in its warfare, however, due to the nature of the operation, it made more sense. As a result 5,000 troops would manage to take a major portion of Al-Immír with relative ease, being granted cover by heavy artillery fire and air support.  

  The war against Al-Immír would take a positive turn by the end of the fourth week since the treaty, with local tribal leaders seeking a peace deal with Thýven, primarily due to mass crop burnings which had been instituted by Thýven through the usage of Agent Orange and White Phosphorus. Unfortunately for the leaders, Thýven wasnt seeking a peace deal, it needed their lands. The matter would escalate once again at the treaty signing when the village leaders were arrested by Thýven Military Police and the dissolution of the region as an independent entity would be declared. 

Thýven had now shaken its fist at West Shamat, and would continue to do so if those on West Shamat continued to attempt to defy the natural right of the Thrømm to expand. Or so the propaganda stated.
